item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q020_syntaxin_fragment_reclassification","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, the fragment structures d1br0a_ and d1ez3a_/d1ez3b_/d1ez3c_, and the full-chain structure d1dn1b_, all have SCCS a.47.2.1. Thus they are not merely independent examples of the all-alpha class (a) or STAT-like fold (a.47), levels that alone do not establish homology: SCOPe places them in the t-SNARE superfamily (a.47.2, probable common ancestry) and, more strongly, the same t-SNARE family (a.47.2.1, close homology). The historical fragment assignments should therefore be interpreted as partial observations of the syntaxin architecture that are anchored by the complete syntaxin chain, not as evidence that the fragments constitute a separate fold. The limitation remains substantial: 1br0 A and 1ez3 A contain only 120 and 127 residues, versus 267 residues in 1dn1 B, so they are suitable templates only for their covered, correctly aligned regions and cannot establish the full-domain topology, long-range contacts, or closed-complex conformation. SCOPe also puts 1dn1 B under an 'automated matches' protein node, so its family assignment is not independent manual protein-level evidence, and family membership alone does not justify transferring exact interaction partners, regulation, or biochemical function without full-length sequence/domain-boundary validation and functional evidence. For representative or modeling use, 1dn1 is obsolete and replaced by the revised, non-obsolete 3c98 structure; d3c98b_ retains a.47.2.1, although its Munc18a-bound context must still be considered.","evidence_used":["/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1br0","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1ez3","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1dn1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1br0/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1ez3/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1dn1/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1br0a_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1ez3a_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1dn1b_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47664","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/311131","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47663","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/191190","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47662","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47661","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47654","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/46456","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/3c98","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/3c98/domains","/api/v1/sequences/pdb/1br0/chains/A?release=2.08","/api/v1/sequences/pdb/1ez3/chains/A?release=2.08","/api/v1/sequences/pdb/1dn1/chains/B?release=2.08","/api/v1/sequences/pdb/3c98/chains/B?release=2.08"]}]}
